unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 9 (AFTER PREP)-LEVEL: B2.1 - THEME 1: SCHOOL LIFE & EDUCATION

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will explore the theme ''School Life and Education'' with a specific focus for comparing different school systems (both local and international), different education systems, and also school traditions, events, and celebrations. Students will research and prepare a multimedia presentation by comparing the structure, curriculum, and teaching methods of schools in their country with those in another country of their choice. They will also examine how schools around the world celebrate national days, festivals, and other events. The project will include visual aids such as posters or slides, and also a reflection on how these traditions and systems shape student experiences and learning. Finally, students will offer their own ideas for a new event or celebration that could enrich school life and develop cultural understanding. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''school life and education with its components such as Comparing different school systems (local and international); comparing different education systems; school traditions, events, and celebration activities; national days and celebrations'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the after prep year 9 of an upper secondary school may know what Comparing different school systems (local and international); comparing different education systems; school traditions, events, and celebration activities; national days and celebrations mean in their as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the after prep year 9 year of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''school life and education'' and also some necessary structures in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in the after prep year 9 of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''school life and education with its components such as Comparing different school systems (local and international); comparing different education systems; school traditions, events, and celebration activities; national days and celebrations'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Their knowledge of the days of the week and holidays will help them learn and practise important national holidays such as ''the Republic Day of Türkiye''. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To write about school systems and school traditions in English through a discussion activity by using target vocabulary and grammar. Activity 1: School Systems and Events Students write a short paragraph to compare two school systems (e.g. local and international) using words such as ''schedule, curriculum, and diversity'' and phrases such as ''unlike, in comparison, and whereas''. Next, they describe a school event they create, such as a talent show or cultural fair; they use target vocabulary such as ''organise, perform'' and descriptive words such as ''collaborative, competitive, traditional''. Students share their work with their classmates for feedback, and the teacher checks their use of language including target vocabulary and grammar and provides constructive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To describe different school systems and school traditions in English through a matching activity by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Vocabulary and Grammar Booster Students work in a vocabulary matching game for different school systems and school traditions by working on target vocabulary and grammar. In pairs, they match vocabulary cards (e.g. schedule, curriculum, celebration, tradition) with their corresponding definitions or example sentences (e.g. ''A planned series of events or tasks for a school day'' for schedule), supported by visual aids and example contexts. Next, they will complete sentences by selecting the correct verb form to make a difference between the Simple Present (e.g. ''The teacher organises a book fair every year'') and the Present Progressive Tense (e.g. ''The students are attending a talent show now''). Throughout the activities, the teacher will observe and encourage students to read their answers aloud. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
